newsitem.title: PERU: Peru leader's popularity hits lowest level.
newsitem.headline: Peru leader's popularity hits lowest level.

text.p: The popularity of Peru's President Alberto Fujimori has fallen to the lowest level in his seven-year rule because of his perceived authoritarianism, according to a poll published on Monday.
Only 27 percent of Peruvians polled said they approved of Fujimori, while 67.8 percent disapproved, according to the survey by respected local pollster Analysts and Consultants.

That contrasted with an average approval rating of 70 percent in polls soon after his successful defeat two months ago of the rebels of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) holding 72 hostages in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.

"Authoritarianism is the main cause for the fall in popularity," Bernardo Verjovsky, director of Analysts and Consultants, said. "When you ask those who reject Fujimori why, most reply, 'Because he is a dictator.'"

Formerly popular for his economic reforms and virtual defeat of leftist guerrillas, Fujimori has antagonized the public in recent weeks with his government's moves against the nation's highest constitutional court and the opposition press.

The government-controlled Congress' dismissal of three Constitutional Tribunal judges who were blocking a possible third election bid by Fujimori in 2000 triggered a wave of street protests throughout the country.
The poll of 400 Peruvians, with a margin of error of plus or minus 4.9 percentage points, also showed that if elections were held now, only 14.5 percent would vote for Fujimori.
The majority, 37 percent, would back increasingly popular Lima Mayor Alberto Andrade, while 12 percent would vote for former U.N. Secretary-General Javier Perez de Cuellar.
Perez de Cuellar, who was defeated by Fujimori in 1995 elections, leads Peru's opposition.
